ev.may_m_tamales.text: In the morning the house smells of steam and maize: tamales wrapped in leaves are cooking over the hearth. You got the first one - hot, with beans and chili.
ev.may_m_cacao_foam.text: A servant poured the cacao from one vessel to another from arm’s height until a thick foam rose on top. Bitter, spiced, with chili - the drink of gods and nobles.
ev.may_m_milpa_burn.text: At the end of the dry season the felled forest was burned for a new milpa. Smoke hung over the jungle for days, and even the sun turned orange.
ev.may_m_planting_stick.text: With a digging stick: a hole, four kernels, a press of the heel. And so on until sunset, row after row, with the sun burning your back.
ev.may_m_turkey_dog.text: Turkeys strut about the yard, and a small hairless dog follows you everywhere. You don’t know yet that it is being fattened for a feast.
ev.may_m_howlers.text: Before dawn the howler monkeys roared in the forest - as loud as jaguars fighting at your very door. Then they fell silent and the birds began to sing.
ev.may_m_jaguar_tracks.text: In the wet earth at the edge of the milpa: jaguar tracks as big as your palm. In the night it passed right by your huts.
ev.may_m_cross_eyed_bead.text: A little bead was tied to your forehead so that your eyes would turn slightly towards your nose. People say that is the most beautiful look - like the maize god’s.
ev.may_m_jade_teeth.text: A craftsman drilled little holes in your front teeth and set discs of jade in them. It hurt, but now your smile is green, like a noble’s.
ev.may_m_tikal_temples.text: From a tall temple above Tikal’s Great Plaza you can see the white roof-combs of other pyramids rising out of the morning mist above the canopy, like islands in a green sea.
ev.may_m_reservoir.text: By the end of the dry season the water in the city reservoir has dropped so low that the plastered bottom shows. People stand with their jars and silently look at the sky.
ev.may_m_bajo.text: The rains have come, and the swampy bajos around Calakmul have filled into a shallow lake. Water stands among the trees, and maize is carried to the city by canoe.
ev.may_m_sacbe.text: You walked at night along a sakbe, a white road of packed lime plaster. Under the moon it glows, and you cannot get lost even in the deepest forest.
ev.may_m_palenque_water.text: The Otolum stream runs under the palace through a stone aqueduct and comes out again in cascades. Children splash in the pools, and the water is cold even in the heat.
ev.may_m_usumacinta.text: On the Usumacinta long canoes went past, loaded with salt and baskets of cacao. The paddlers sang in rhythm, and the bow of the boat was painted with eyes.
ev.may_m_copan_stelae.text: In Copán’s Great Plaza stand stelae painted red. The kings on them seem to step out of the stone, and glyphs that only a few can read wind along their sides.
ev.may_m_copan_macaws.text: Scarlet macaws flew screeching over the Copán valley - red, yellow and blue like the paint on a temple. People say they are the birds of the sun itself.
ev.may_m_market.text: At the market a handful of cacao beans buys chili, and a cotton mantle buys flint knives and obsidian blades. The salt seller shouts louder than anyone.
ev.may_m_obsidian_cut.text: An obsidian blade is the sharpest thing in the world - you learned that when it slid across your finger. The bleeding took a long time to stop.
ev.may_m_ballgame_watch.text: On the ballcourt the heavy rubber ball bounced off the players’ hips with a dull thud. No one may touch it with their hands, and the crowd gasped at every hit against the sloping wall.
ev.may_m_painted_vase.text: You watched a scribe paint a cylinder vase with a fine brush: court scenes, and around the rim a line of glyphs naming the owner and the word "cacao".
ev.may_m_first_rain.text: After the long drought the first rain poured down. The grown-ups stood in it with their faces turned up, and the children danced in the puddles: Chaak had heard.
ev.may_m_sweatbath.text: In the cramped stone sweatbath someone poured water on the hot stones. Herb-scented steam, heat down to the bones - and then cool water from a jar.
ev.may_m_cotton_spindle.text: You are learning to spin cotton: the spindle with its clay whorl twirls in a gourd bowl, and the thread keeps breaking. The older women laugh - theirs broke too.
ev.may_m_backstrap.text: One end of the backstrap loom is tied to a tree, the other to your back. Lean back a little and the threads go taut. By evening there is a pattern of diamonds on the loom.
ev.may_m_chultun.text: You helped clean the chultun, the bottle-shaped underground cistern by the house where rainwater runs off the roof. Without it no one would last the dry season.
ev.may_m_venus.text: An old man by the fire pointed to a bright star near the horizon. "That is Chak Ek’, the Great Star. When it returns, kings go to war." You couldn’t sleep for a long time.
ev.may_m_house_floor.text: Beneath the floor of your house lie the ancestors, each with a jade bead in the mouth and a bowl beside them. In the evenings the grown-ups talk to them as if they were alive.
ev.may_m_stucco_mask.text: The temple has been renewed for the festival: the huge stucco masks of the gods on the stairway are freshly painted red, their eyes black. From afar they seem to watch you.
ev.may_m_feather_dance.text: Dancers wearing enormous feathered backracks whirled to drums and conch-shell trumpets. The quetzal plumes shimmered green and gold in the sunset.
ev.may_m_captive_water.text: Before dawn you carry heavy jars from the reservoir. On the steps of the noble house no one sees you - just as no one sees a shadow.
ev.may_m_captive_language.text: A new captive in the master’s house spoke to you in the speech of your home town. You whispered half the night away - about the river, the houses, the songs.
ev.may_m_drought_dust.text: Where your grandfather’s maize once rustled there is now dust and low scrub. The soil has slid off the slopes, and stones stick out like bones.
ev.may_m_empty_houses.text: Another house on your street stands empty: the neighbours have left, abandoning the hearth and the cracked pots. Grass is already sprouting on the roof.
ev.may_m_mosquitoes.text: The rainy season: everything is damp, the mats are mouldy, and the mosquitoes whine all night. Only the smoke of smouldering leaves helps.
ev.may_m_tapir.text: By the river a tapir stepped out of the thicket - heavy, with its little trunk - and calmly walked into the water as if you weren’t there.
ev.may_m_scribe_numbers.text: You were shown how to count the local way: a dot is one, a bar is five, a shell is zero. You laid out the number of your years in maize kernels.
ev.may_m_copal.text: Before dawn copal is burned at the shrine. The white, resin-scented smoke rises to the sky: it is food for the gods.
ev.may_d_tribute.title: Tribute for the court
ev.may_d_tribute.text: The sajal’s men are going from house to house: the court needs cotton mantles, cacao and maize. A scribe with a brush notes down who brought what.
ev.may_d_tribute.hide.success: The collectors didn’t look into the cistern. You got away with it.
ev.may_d_tribute.hide.failure: A neighbour pointed out the hiding place. You had to pay double and put up with sideways looks.
ev.may_d_tribute.plead.success: The scribe listened and struck off part of the debt: it really was a bad year.
ev.may_d_tribute.plead.failure: "Everyone says that," they told you, and took it all.
ev.may_d_corvee.title: Building the temple
ev.may_d_corvee.text: The lord means to raise a new temple over the old one: as custom demands, the old one will be sealed inside. Hands are needed to haul stone, burn lime and carry water - for the whole dry season.
ev.may_d_corvee.substitute: Buy your way out with cacao
ev.may_d_corvee.flee: Slip into the forest until the levy is over
ev.may_d_corvee.flee.success: You waited it out in a forest hamlet. No one noticed you were gone.
ev.may_d_corvee.flee.failure: They found you and marched you back under guard. You had to work twice as hard.
ev.may_d_corvee_remembered.title: A long memory
ev.may_d_corvee_remembered.text: The overseer of that old building project has become an important man at court. He hasn’t forgotten who ran away, and now somehow none of your affairs ever get settled.
ev.may_d_ball_bet.title: Wagers on the ball
ev.may_d_ball_bet.text: A big match: your district’s team against visitors from a neighbouring city. The nobles wager jade, feathers and mantles; ordinary folk bet handfuls of cacao.
ev.may_d_ball_bet.big.success: The ball went through the stone ring! You carried home a whole basket of cacao.
ev.may_d_ball_bet.big.failure: Your side lost. You walked home in silence and much lighter.
ev.may_d_ball_bet.small.success: You won a little - just enough for festive tamales.
ev.may_d_ball_bet.small.failure: The handful is gone. No matter.
ev.may_d_first_blood.title: First blood for the gods
ev.may_d_first_blood.text: It is time for you to give your blood to the gods for the first time: a stingray spine, strips of bark paper to catch the drops, and the smoke in which, they say, the ancestors appear to the living. All your kin are watching.
ev.may_d_first_blood.endure.success: You didn’t flinch. In the copal smoke you thought you saw a serpent with a human face. The elders nodded with approval.
ev.may_d_first_blood.endure.failure: Your head spun and you collapsed right by the altar. People will whisper about it.
ev.may_d_bride_service.title: Serving for a bride
ev.may_d_bride_service.text: The matchmaker has arranged it: the girl is willing and so is her family. But by custom the groom lives in the bride’s house for some years and works for her family until he proves he is no idler.
ev.may_d_bride_service.serve: Live with her kin and work
ev.may_d_bride_service_end.title: The service is done
ev.may_d_bride_service_end.text: Your years of work for your wife’s family are over. Your father-in-law called you his son in front of everyone, gave you maize and cacao, and helped you raise a house of your own.
ev.may_d_scribe_lessons.title: A scribe’s pupil
ev.may_d_scribe_lessons.text: A scribe from the palace workshop is looking for a pupil. First come years of grinding pigments and trimming brushes, then glyphs, the count of days and the names of the gods. Few are taught to write.
ev.may_d_scribe_offer.title: A place in the workshop
ev.may_d_scribe_offer.text: Your old teacher kept his word: you are invited into the court scribes’ workshop to paint vessels and keep records for the lord.
ev.may_d_tired_milpa.title: A tired field
ev.may_d_tired_milpa.text: The third year in the same place - and the maize only reaches your waist instead of over your head. The old men say the field is tired and needs ten years of rest. But there is less and less free forest near the city.
ev.may_d_tired_milpa.clear_new: Clear a new plot farther away
ev.may_d_tired_milpa.terraces: Build stone terraces on the slope
ev.may_d_tired_milpa.keep.success: The rains were generous, and the field fed the family one more time.
ev.may_d_tired_milpa.keep.failure: The harvest was miserable. You had to borrow to last until the next crop.
ev.may_d_terraces_pay.title: The terraces hold
ev.may_d_terraces_pay.text: The downpours washed the soil off your neighbours’ slopes, but your terraces held. Behind the stone walls the maize stands thick - the neighbours come to look and ask you to teach them.
ev.may_d_salt_trip.title: To the sea for salt
ev.may_d_salt_trip.text: Several families are setting off to the coast for salt - many days on foot there and back, with baskets carried by a strap across the forehead. In the forest salt is worth more than anything but jade.
ev.may_d_salt_trip.go.success: You came back with a heavy basket of salt and traded it well at the market.
ev.may_d_salt_trip.go.failure: On the way a fever laid you low. You had to give away the salt for shelter and herbs.
ev.may_d_dayname.title: The day of your birth
ev.may_d_dayname.text: The daykeeper scattered seeds and crystals on a mat and counted for a long time by the sacred calendar of two hundred and sixty days. Your birth day, he said, is a Wind day: your life will be restless, but people will listen to your voice.
ev.may_d_buy_captive.title: A captive for sale
ev.may_d_buy_captive.text: After a raid the warriors are selling captives: a young man from an enemy city who speaks a strange dialect and stares at the ground. He could carry water and work your fields.
ev.may_d_buy_captive.free: Buy him and let him go home
ev.may_d_captive_loyal.title: A loyal servant
ev.may_d_captive_loyal.text: The captive you once bought caught a thief at your storerooms one night. He has long spoken your language and seems to think of this house as his own.
ev.may_d_war_levy.title: A raid
ev.may_d_war_levy.text: The war captain is gathering men: the lord is raiding a neighbouring city and needs captives for the festival and tribute. A spear, a hide shield - and ten days’ march through the forest.
ev.may_d_war_levy.go.success: Your band burst into an enemy village at dawn. You came home with spoils, and people talked about you around the hearths.
ev.may_d_war_levy.go.failure: An ambush at the ford. You came back with a spear wound and no spoils.
ev.may_d_war_levy.hide.success: The band left without you. No one came looking.
ev.may_d_war_levy.hide.failure: They found you and called you a coward in front of everyone. You had to pay.
ev.may_d_feast_host.title: A feast for allies
ev.may_d_feast_host.text: It is time for your family to give a feast: to invite kin, allies and people of the court. Frothy cacao in painted vessels, turkeys, venison, balché, musicians. No one trusts a host who doesn’t feed his guests.
ev.may_d_feast_host.lavish: A feast for the whole city
ev.may_d_feast_returned.title: A debt of hospitality
ev.may_d_feast_returned.text: A guest from that long-ago feast has risen at court. He remembers your generosity: he sent cotton mantles, cacao, and put in a word for you with the lord.
ev.may_d_name_vase.title: A vessel with your name
ev.may_d_name_vase.text: The best scribe in the city will paint a cacao vessel for you: a court scene and a line of glyphs - "this is the drinking vessel of so-and-so, the noble". It will be handed down in the family and then laid in your grave.
ev.may_d_reservoir_work.title: Cleaning the reservoir
ev.may_d_reservoir_work.text: While the water is low, the whole district turns out to clean the reservoir: scoop out the silt, patch the plaster floor, cut the reeds. Without this water the city won’t last until the rains.
ev.may_d_reservoir_work.pay: Send a basket of maize instead
ev.may_d_green_obsidian.title: Traders from the west
ev.may_d_green_obsidian.text: Traders have come to the market from the far mountain lands in the west, where a great city stands with pyramids of the Sun and Moon. They carry green obsidian, which is never found here, and foreign gods on their shields.
ev.may_d_green_obsidian.buy.success: The nobles snapped up the green blades at three times the price.
ev.may_d_green_obsidian.buy.failure: Half the blades cracked on the way. You barely got your cacao back.
ev.may_d_deer_hunt.title: A deer hunt
ev.may_d_deer_hunt.text: The men are gathering for a hunt: spears, blowguns, dogs. A deer is needed for the festival - and everyone craves meat after months of beans and maize.
ev.may_d_deer_hunt.join.success: Your spear struck first. You got the best share.
ev.may_d_deer_hunt.join.failure: You slipped off a rock in a ravine and came home limping.
ev.may_d_snakebite.title: A snake in the grass
ev.may_d_snakebite.text: You didn’t see the fer-de-lance in the leaves. A bite on the ankle - your leg burns and swells before your eyes.
ev.may_d_snakebite.healer.success: The healer cut the wound, applied herbs and whispered spells all night. You pulled through.
ev.may_d_snakebite.healer.failure: Even the healer couldn’t stop the fever. You were laid up for a long time.
ev.may_d_snakebite.herbs.success: A neighbour knew the right root. Within a week you were walking again.
ev.may_d_snakebite.herbs.failure: The swelling crept up to your knee. You are shaking with fever.
ev.may_d_snakebite.pray.success: By morning the pain had eased. Clearly the gods aren’t calling you yet.
ev.may_d_snakebite.pray.failure: The prayers didn’t help. You are burning with fever.
ev.may_d_captive_ransom.title: Talk of ransom
ev.may_d_captive_ransom.text: In the master’s house people whisper: envoys from your home city have come to make peace. They say some of the captives may be ransomed for jade and mantles.
ev.may_d_captive_ransom.plead: Throw yourself at the envoys’ feet
ev.may_d_captive_ransom.plead.success: The envoy recognised your family and put you on the list. You are free!
ev.may_d_captive_ransom.plead.failure: The guards dragged you away before you could finish speaking.
ev.may_d_ransom_freed.title: Going home
ev.may_d_ransom_freed.text: Your name was on the list of the ransomed. You walk the white road towards home, and every step feels strange, as if you were learning to walk again.
ev.may_d_court_guest.title: A guest at a foreign court
ev.may_d_court_guest.text: The overlord invites young men and women of subject families to his court - "as guests". Everyone understands: it is both an honour and a pledge of loyalty.
ev.may_d_court_guest_return.title: Friends at court
ev.may_d_court_guest_return.text: Your years at the foreign court were not wasted. One of the lords there, with whom you learned dances and speeches, has become your patron.
ev.may_d_drought_store.title: Drought again
ev.may_d_drought_store.text: For the third year the rains come late and leave early. The maize is small, prices are rising, and the priests say the gods are angry. What will you do with what you have?
ev.may_d_drought_store.store: Store grain in the underground pits
ev.may_d_cacao_grove.title: A cacao grove
ev.may_d_cacao_grove.text: In a damp hollow by the stream you could plant cacao. The trees need shade and years of patience: the first pods will come in five years or so. But cacao is both a drink and money.
ev.may_d_cacao_harvest.title: The first pods
ev.may_d_cacao_harvest.text: Yellow and red pods hang from the trunks of your trees. The beans are drying on mats, and the smell carries across the whole neighbourhood. This is wealth that grows by itself.
ev.may_d_apprentice_jade.title: The jade master
ev.may_d_apprentice_jade.text: An old jade carver is looking for a patient apprentice. Jade isn’t cut with a knife but with a cord, sand and water, for weeks on end. But a single bead is worth a whole field’s harvest.
ev.may_t_captured.title: A raid at dawn
ev.may_t_captured.text: At dawn warriors of a foreign lord burst into the village: painted faces, war cries, burning roofs. They want captives - alive.
ev.may_t_captured.fight.success: You drove them off. The raiders left carrying their wounded, and now everyone knows your name.
ev.may_t_captured.fight.failure: You were knocked down and bound. Now you are a captive in a foreign city.
ev.may_t_captured.flee.success: You escaped, but your house and stores burned.
ev.may_t_captured.flee.failure: They caught you at the stream. Now you are a captive.
ev.may_t_noble_captured.title: Taken captive
ev.may_t_noble_captured.text: In battle you were surrounded and taken alive. Noble captives are led through the enemy city, and their fate is decided before the next festival. Your family may offer a ransom - if they are in time.
ev.may_t_noble_captured.ransom.success: Your family gave jade, feathers and mantles. You came home humbled, but alive.
ev.may_t_noble_captured.ransom.failure: The ransom didn’t come in time. You were kept in the enemy city as a captive.
ev.may_t_noble_captured.escape.success: You gnawed through the ropes and slipped away through the forest. They will sing about your escape.
ev.may_t_noble_captured.serve: Swear loyalty to the enemy lord
ev.may_t_jade_cache.title: A cache in the earth
ev.may_t_jade_cache.text: Under a stone by an old mound your stick struck a lid: two bowls placed lip to lip, and inside - jade beads, obsidian blades and a strangely shaped flint. Someone’s ancient offering.
ev.may_t_cache_curse.title: The spirits’ anger
ev.may_t_cache_curse.text: You are tormented by fever and bad dreams. The daykeeper, not meeting your eyes, said: the one whose offering you sold has come to collect.
ev.may_t_lord_notice.title: Noticed at court
ev.may_t_lord_notice.text: At the festival the lord noticed you - for your skill, or for a clever word - and ordered you taken into his household. For a commoner it is an unheard-of rise.
ev.may_t_court_intrigue.title: A storm at the palace
ev.may_t_court_intrigue.text: At court two families are fighting for the lord’s favour, and your patron has ended up on the losing side. New people without a lineage are the first to go.
ev.may_t_court_intrigue.loyal.success: The storm passed you by, and your loyalty was remembered.
ev.may_t_court_intrigue.loyal.failure: You were thrown out of the palace and stripped of almost everything.
ev.may_t_court_intrigue.leave: Slip away quietly while you can
ev.may_t_sorcery.title: Accused of sorcery
ev.may_t_sorcery.text: A neighbour’s child has died, and the mother screams down the street that you sent the sickness: you were seen near their house at night. People look away.
ev.may_t_sorcery.judgment.success: The aj k’in cast the seeds and declared that the sickness came from a god’s anger, not from you. The neighbours fell silent.
ev.may_t_sorcery.judgment.failure: The signs went against you. You had to pay for a cleansing and endure the curses.
ev.may_t_sorcery.pay: Pay off the family with gifts
ev.may_t_hurricane.title: A storm from the sea
ev.may_t_hurricane.text: In the night a hurricane came. The wind tore off thatched roofs and felled trees, and the maize lay flat in every field. In the morning the village looks as if a giant had walked through it.
ev.may_t_hurricane.move: Go to kin in another city
ev.may_t_hurricane.ask_lord.success: The lord opened his storehouses. You received a share of maize.
ev.may_t_hurricane.ask_lord.failure: There were hundreds of petitioners at court. No one even heard you out.
ev.may_t_house_fire.title: Fire
ev.may_t_house_fire.text: A spark from the hearth caught the dry thatch. A moment later the fire has leapt to the next house, where old people and children are sleeping.
ev.may_t_house_fire.goods.success: You dragged out the baskets and sacks before the roof fell in.
ev.may_t_house_fire.goods.failure: The roof caved in while you were inside. The burns will hurt for a long time.
ev.may_t_house_fire.people: Wake the neighbours and get them out
ev.may_t_robbed.title: Ambush on the trail
ev.may_t_robbed.text: On a forest trail between cities armed men stepped out of the thicket. The porters dropped their baskets and pressed against the trees. In front of you lies a whole season’s jade, salt and cacao.
ev.may_t_robbed.fight.success: The robbers fled, leaving their own goods behind. The porters look at you with admiration.
ev.may_t_robbed.fight.failure: You were knocked out with a club. You came to with nothing left.
ev.may_t_robbed.bargain.success: You talked them into taking a little and letting you pass: "Kill a trader and no one will come this way again."
ev.may_t_robbed.bargain.failure: The talk only made them angry. They took almost everything.
ev.may_t_adopted.title: Another lineage
ev.may_t_adopted.text: A childless sajal your family once worked for wants to take you into his house as his ward and heir. A new name, new kin, a different life.
ev.may_t_master_dies.title: The master’s death
ev.may_t_master_dies.text: The master is dead. His heir wants to sell you to traders bound for a distant city, but the widow you have served for many years says you have earned your freedom. It will all be decided before the mourning ends.
ev.may_t_master_dies.plead: Ask the widow to speak for you
ev.may_t_master_dies.plead.success: The widow got her way. You are free - and you have a scrap of land.
ev.may_t_master_dies.plead.failure: The heir proved stronger. You were led away with a caravan to a foreign city.
ev.may_t_master_dies.run: Run while everyone is busy with the funeral
ev.may_t_master_dies.run.success: You slipped through the forest to a distant village where no one knows you. You are free.
ev.may_t_master_dies.run.failure: They caught you on the second day.
ev.may_t_inherit.title: An inheritance from distant kin
ev.may_t_inherit.text: A distant relative, a sajal from a neighbouring town, has died without direct heirs. By lineage law his estates could pass to you - but his son-in-law is already living in his house.
ev.may_t_inherit.claim.success: The council of elders recognised your right. Now you have lands and people.
ev.may_t_inherit.claim.failure: The son-in-law was in favour at court. You lost and made an enemy.
ev.may_t_inherit.share: Come to terms and split it
ev.may_j_join_warriors.title: Into the lord’s war band
ev.may_j_join_warriors.text: The lord’s war captain is choosing young men for his standing war band: quilted cotton armour, a flint-tipped spear, food from the palace fields. In return - raids and war.
ev.may_j_ball_trial.title: A trial on the ballcourt
ev.may_j_ball_trial.text: You struck the ball with your hip so skilfully at a village game that an old player from the city team invited you to a trial. Pitz is the game of the gods, but also a trade: players are fed by noble patrons.
ev.may_j_ball_trial.refuse: It’s a pastime, not a living
ev.may_j_daykeeper_call.title: The daykeeper’s call
ev.may_j_daykeeper_call.text: The old aj k’in says he saw you in a dream holding a bundle of seeds and crystals: the gods have chosen you to count the days. The training is long - the two hundred and sixty days of the sacred year, the stars, the names of the gods.
ev.may_j_healer_pupil.title: A healer’s pupil
ev.may_j_healer_pupil.text: The healer woman at the edge of the village has noticed that you remember herbs after seeing them once, and she asks you to be her pupil: roots for fever, bark for the flux, spells against snakebite.
ev.may_j_scribe_vase.title: An order for the court
ev.may_j_scribe_vase.text: The court has ordered twenty painted vessels as festival gifts for its allies. Each needs a reception scene and a line of glyphs with the lord’s titles. The deadline is short.
ev.may_j_scribe_vase.fast: Finish everything and take another order
ev.may_j_scribe_vase.fast.success: You managed both. Your hands are shaking, but you’ll have cacao for a long time.
ev.may_j_scribe_vase.fast.failure: In your haste you got a glyph wrong in the lord’s name. They smashed the vessel in front of you.
ev.may_j_scribe_promote.title: Keeper of the books
ev.may_j_scribe_promote.text: The old aj k’uhuun, keeper of the lord’s sacred books, has gone blind. The court needs a new one: to keep the bark-paper books, count the tribute and remember who owes whom and how much.
ev.may_j_ball_big.title: The match against the visitors
ev.may_j_ball_big.text: The lord is receiving envoys from a neighbouring city, and in their honour there will be a great match. The ball is heavy as a stone, and the court is full of nobles. To lose in front of guests would shame the whole city.
ev.may_j_ball_big.all_in.success: Your hip strike decided the game. The nobles showered you with feathers and beads.
ev.may_j_ball_big.all_in.failure: The ball hit you in the side and something cracked. You were carried off the court.
ev.may_j_ball_patron.title: A noble patron
ev.may_j_ball_patron.text: A lord who has bet on you many times invites you to join his team: you’ll eat from his table, and he’ll pay for your gear - the yoke-belt, the kneepad, the feathers.
ev.may_j_jade_mask.title: The funeral mask
ev.may_j_jade_mask.text: The court needs a jade mosaic mask for a noble’s burial: hundreds of plaques, eyes of shell and obsidian. A year of work, and no mistakes allowed - the face will gaze on the gods forever.
ev.may_j_jade_mask.accept.success: The mask came out as if alive. They say it was shown to the lord himself.
ev.may_j_jade_mask.accept.failure: The plaques cracked one after another. The order was given to another master.
ev.may_j_own_workshop.title: Apprentices of your own
ev.may_j_own_workshop.text: Three young people at once are asking to be your apprentices, and you have more orders than you can manage. You could take over an annex by the palace and become a master with apprentices.
ev.may_j_salt_canoe.title: The water route
ev.may_j_salt_canoe.text: Traders from the coast offer you a share in a great canoe: salt, shells and cotton along the shore, and from there up the rivers. Twice as fast as going on foot - if no storm catches you.
ev.may_j_salt_canoe.go.success: The canoe arrived without loss. Your share was more than a year of journeys on foot.
ev.may_j_salt_canoe.go.failure: A storm overturned the canoe near the shore. You swam out; the salt did not.
ev.may_j_warrior_captive.title: A captive for the lord
ev.may_j_warrior_captive.text: In the press of battle you see an enemy lord in a feathered headdress: to seize him by the hair is to take a captive worthy of a stela. But a wounded comrade has fallen beside you.
ev.may_j_warrior_captive.seize.success: You brought the noble captive to the lord’s feet. You were given a new title-name.
ev.may_j_warrior_captive.seize.failure: The lord was stronger than you, and his bodyguards were closer.
ev.may_j_officer_promote.title: A band of your own
ev.may_j_officer_promote.text: The lord remembers your captives. He gives you a shield painted with a jaguar and a hundred warriors: now you lead them on raids.
ev.may_j_priest_katun.title: The prophecy of the k’atun
ev.may_j_priest_katun.text: The end of the k’atun, the twenty-year cycle, is near. You count the days and the stars, and everything speaks of drought and strife. The lord awaits a prophecy that can be carved on a stela.
ev.may_j_priest_katun.truth.success: The lord listened and ordered maize to be stored. When the drought came, people called you wise.
ev.may_j_priest_katun.truth.failure: The lord was furious: "You prophesy disaster for my k’atun?" You were barred from the rites.
ev.may_j_priest_katun.soften: Say what they want to hear
ev.may_j_healer_noble.title: A noble child’s illness
ev.may_j_healer_noble.text: In the night they sent for you from the palace: the sajal’s little daughter has a fever and fits. The priests have already made offerings; now it is the healer’s turn. If the child dies, you will be blamed.
ev.may_j_healer_noble.treat.success: A bark brew and cold wraps broke the fever by dawn. The sajal sent you mantles and cacao.
ev.may_j_healer_noble.treat.failure: The child recovered, but people say it was the priests who helped and you only got in the way.
ev.may_j_stone_stela.title: A stela for the lord
ev.may_j_stone_stela.text: For the period ending the lord is raising a new stela. The scribe has already drawn the design in charcoal - the king in a feathered headdress and columns of glyphs. You are trusted to carve the face.
ev.may_j_stone_stela.carve.success: The face came out so alive that the lord stood silent for a long time, then smiled.
ev.may_j_stone_stela.carve.failure: The chisel slipped, and the nose had to be patched with plaster. Everyone noticed.
ev.may_j_stone_stela.assist: Leave it to the senior master
ev.may_j_feather_quetzal.title: Quetzal feathers
ev.may_j_feather_quetzal.text: Traders have come down from the southern mountains with long green quetzal plumes - they are plucked from the living bird, which is then set free. A royal headdress needs hundreds of them.
ev.may_j_feather_quetzal.buy.success: The court itself bought the headdress made from these plumes.
ev.may_j_feather_quetzal.buy.failure: Half the plumes turned out to be dyed parrot feathers.
ev.may_j_overseer.title: Overseer of captives
ev.may_j_overseer.text: The master has noticed that your work goes well and wants to put you in charge of the other captives in his fields. You’ll eat better - but you’ll be an outsider among them.
ev.may_j_rapids.title: The rapids
ev.may_j_rapids.text: The Usumacinta is running high, and the rapids are roaring. The head paddler wants to run them straight away rather than haul the canoe and cargo along the bank for a whole day.
ev.may_j_rapids.run.success: The canoe shot through, shipping water over the side. You arrived a day early.
ev.may_j_rapids.run.failure: The boat struck a rock. They pulled you out of the water half-dead.
ev.may_j_rapids.portage: Carry it round on the bank
ev.may_j_first_ears.title: The first ears
ev.may_j_first_ears.text: The first young ears of maize are ripe. By custom they are carried to a little altar in the field for the maize god, who dies and is reborn every year with the grain.
ev.may_j_first_ears.offer: Give the best to the god
ev.may_j_first_ears.keep: Keep them to eat - it’s a hard year
ev.may_mv_to_tikal.title: The call of Tikal
ev.may_mv_to_tikal.text: A kinsman who moved to Tikal long ago has sent word with the traders: the great city needs hands, its markets are louder and its temples taller. He will help you settle.
ev.may_mv_to_calakmul.title: To the Snake capital
ev.may_mv_to_calakmul.text: Tribute flows into Calakmul from all over the lowlands, and the court of the Snake kingdom always needs craftsmen, scribes and traders. You are offered a place with one of the sajals.
ev.may_mv_copan_school.title: To study in Copán
ev.may_mv_copan_school.text: They say that in Copán stone is carved so that the kings step almost entirely out of the stelae, and the scribes know glyphs that even the old men here have forgotten. It is a long journey south.
ev.may_mv_to_palenque.title: The city of Big Water
ev.may_mv_to_palenque.text: The traders talk about Palenque: streams run right through the city, the land by the river yields richly, and at the court of Pakal’s heirs they build marvels. A canoe leaves for there in a few days.
ev.may_mv_leave_city.title: The city is emptying
ev.may_mv_leave_city.text: No new stelae have been raised for years, the court has grown poor, and the rains are stingy. Every week someone bundles up their belongings and leaves - for forest villages, for kin in other cities, or far to the north, where new cities are said to be growing.
ev.may_mv_leave_city.north: Go north to the Puuc hills
ev.may_mv_leave_city.other: Go to kin in another city
ev.may_mv_noble_bride.title: A bride for an alliance
ev.may_mv_noble_bride.text: The lord of another city has asked for your hand. This marriage will seal an alliance between two dynasties: noble women have often gone to foreign cities this way - and sometimes ruled there themselves.
ev.may_mv_noble_bride.plead.success: Your family gave way: the alliance will be sealed some other way.
ev.may_mv_noble_bride.plead.failure: The lord’s word has been given. A month later you were sent off with gifts to the foreign city.
ev.may_f_chaak.title: Asking for rain
ev.may_f_chaak.text: The rains are a month late. The village gathers at the altar on the edge of the milpa: the old men call on Chaak, the rain god with the lightning axe, and the boys croak like frogs - his messengers.
ev.may_f_chaak.blood: Give a drop of your own blood
ev.may_f_chaak.nothing: The rain will come on its own
ev.may_f_vision.title: The vision serpent
ev.may_f_vision.text: After a fast and a sleepless night the priest hands you a brew and a stingray spine. They say that in the smoke of burning bark spattered with blood a serpent rises, and from its jaws an ancestor emerges with words for the living.
ev.may_f_cave.title: Pilgrimage to the cave
ev.may_f_cave.text: Caves are doorways to Xibalba, the underworld, where the rain gods and the ancestors dwell. Pilgrims walk to the sacred cave in the hills with torches and copal, and on its walls scribes leave names and dates.
ev.may_f_period_ending.title: The end of a k’atun
ev.may_f_period_ending.text: A k’atun is ending - twenty years of the Long Count. The lord, in jade and feathers, scatters copal before a new stela, and the whole city brings gifts so the new twenty years will be kind.
ev.may_f_way.title: Your spirit companion
ev.may_f_way.text: You dreamed of a jaguar: it walked beside you through the night forest, and you saw through its eyes. The old people say everyone has a way, a spirit companion, and not everyone ever meets it face to face.
ev.may_f_bury_elder.title: Farewell to an elder
ev.may_f_bury_elder.text: The elder of your lineage has died. He will be buried beneath the floor of the house where he lived, with a bowl of food for the long road through Xibalba. A jade bead is placed in the dead man’s mouth - breath that never ends.
ev.may_f_doubt.title: The gods are silent
ev.may_f_doubt.text: The lord let his own blood, the priests burned copal, captives in the plaza awaited their fate - and still no rain. People whisper more and more: perhaps the holy lord no longer speaks with the gods?
ev.may_f_doubt.village: Go to the old village shrine instead
